items.headline: Stocks claw back part of Thursday's rout, but the tech sell-off isn't over
items.note: Thursday was the Nasdaq's worst day since April 2025 and the Dow fell about 1,800 points; stocks recovered some of that Friday, with the VIX near 24. I couldn't confirm Friday's closing index levels. One strategist says the selling could last another week.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO, likely mid-November, faces a cooler market
items.note: Investors now see a $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion valuation, down from about $2 trillion talked about earlier. Voters rejected 40 of 41 local data-center ballot measures, and the filing lists about $895.4 billion of compute commitments. It would be the first pure-play AI company to list.

items.headline: Microsoft is trimming its 'neocloud' AI capacity partners
items.note: Per CNBC, it plans to focus on fewer suppliers and its own data centers, and two sources say it didn't renew its Oracle deal. CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN shares each fell about half in a month. It's a sign the AI buildout may slow, which affects hiring at AI infrastructure firms.

items.headline: October CPI arrives Tuesday
items.note: Economists expect inflation of 3.9% year over year, up from 3.7%. A hot number would raise odds of Fed rate hikes and could pressure tech stocks again. Producer prices follow Friday.

items.headline: AI is speeding up recruiting and squeezing agency fees
items.note: A Bullhorn survey found 37% of recruiters said AI made screening 26% to 50% faster. Adecco says humans still make the hiring decisions. For applicants, expect more automated screening early in the process.

items.headline: Nvidia lost about $440 billion in value Thursday; earnings come later this month
items.note: The Magnificent Seven lost roughly $1 trillion that day. Nvidia isn't on next week's calendar, so its report is the next big test of AI chip sentiment.

items.headline: OpenAI says it will keep investing in data centers despite the election
items.note: CNBC reports OpenAI executives responded to the post-midterm sell-off, and OpenAI released a data-center policy proposal Thursday. I only saw headlines, not details.

items.headline: Meta executive Dave Wehner leaves to become CFO of AI startup Fireworks
items.note: Per CNBC's Saturday headline, a senior finance leader is moving from Big Tech to an AI infrastructure startup. I didn't read the full story.

items.headline: Take-Two reports earnings Monday
items.note: It's on CNBC's calendar for Nov. 9. Worth watching if you follow game-industry business.

learn.explain: Leverage means using borrowed money to fund growth. It can boost returns when things go well, but the interest still has to be paid when they don't. Many 'neocloud' companies borrowed heavily to buy AI chips and build data centers. When a big customer like Microsoft pulls back, those debts remain, which is part of why CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN shares fell about half in a month. It's also why higher interest rates hurt heavily indebted companies most.
